answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Mirroring. Each identity's action distribution from prior epochs is stored as an opal-profile hash; new epochs must match it within a divergence threshold, checked by peer sampling. A farmed identity can't predict which past behaviours will be queried, so each must be engineered and maintained across epochs. The anchor binding an identity to its history is its cumulative divergence record, which cannot be reset without abandoning accumulated standing.
